attribution: Every model in this corpus was written for APORIA. None of them downloads data, and none is derived from a third-party benchmark file, so there is nothing to attribute and no licence to comply with beyond this one.

provenance.author: Ram Bhogesara
provenance.how: analytic models written in the Aporia DSL, plus mutants produced by changing exactly one line of a clean model, recorded in each entry's `mutant_of` field
provenance.external_families: SciMLBenchmarks, OpenMDAO examples, NASA NTRS and NIST Matrix Market are the intended sources for later entries. None is used yet, so no download, licence check or attribution is claimed here.

families.name: analytic
families.purpose: ground truth is a closed-form property of the real numbers or of IEEE-754, so the true region and its boundary are exact

families.name: ode
families.purpose: step size and rate produce stability boundaries, including a curved one an axis-aligned atlas can only stair-step

families.name: control
families.purpose: the same equations in two update orders, one with a genuine trusted region and one without

families.name: linear_algebra
families.purpose: catastrophic cancellation over a nine-decade parameter range

families.name: aerospace
families.purpose: a clean model used as a false-positive control, and two single-line mutants of it

families.name: electromagnetics
families.purpose: a narrow interior band at a resonance, which is the shape boundary discovery is for

families.name: mutants
families.purpose: fault classes from the specification that APORIA should catch without executing anything

families.name: synthetic
families.purpose: a difficulty ladder: rectangular wells whose declared rule fails inside a box whose volume is exact by construction, so the cost of a search can be plotted against the size of the region rather than against whatever a physical model happens to make hard
families.note: the rule is `max_i(abs(axis_i) - bound_i) > 0`, which is negative exactly inside the box; bounds are inset by 1e-6 of the half-width because a point on a rule boundary has zero violation magnitude. `narrow_1d_unreachable` is deliberately beyond the atlas's depth limit: it measures the resolution of the representation, not the quality of a search.

ground_truth.format: truth.json per entry, declaring axis-aligned boxes as a union, plus the boundary values and the derivation in plain language
ground_truth.why_boxes: a union of boxes is checkable by direct evaluation. Where the true region is curved the entry says so, and the declared boxes are an inner approximation with the exact edge values listed in the derivation.
ground_truth.verification: aporia-bench verifies every declaration against a dense grid evaluation of the model's own declared rules before any search result is reported, and the corpus test fails if a declaration does not hold
